definitions.explanation: The discovery of artifacts, remains, or other items through archaeological excavation. Describes the act of something being dug up from the ground.

examples.japanese: {土器|どき}が{出土|しゅつど}した。
この{遺跡|いせき}から{多|おお}くの{出土|しゅつど}{品|ひん}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: Many excavated artifacts were found at this archaeological site.

examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}から{古代|こだい}の{銅鏡|どうきょう}が{出土|しゅつど}し、{調査|ちょうさ}が{行|おこな}われている。
examples.english: An ancient bronze mirror was unearthed at the construction site, and an investigation is underway.

notes:
Used primarily in archaeological and historical contexts. The subject is typically the item being unearthed, not the person doing the digging. As a する verb: {出土|しゅつど}する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{出土|しゅつど}{品|ひん} (excavated artifact)
・{出土|しゅつど}{遺物|いぶつ} (excavated relic)
・{遺跡|いせき}から{出土|しゅつど}する (be excavated from ruins)
・{大量|たいりょう}に{出土|しゅつど}する (be unearthed in large quantities)
